lines.li: [us] You work as hard as any of us, and you don't have to.
[them,their:empire] At court I would never lift a thing, but the term passes faster this way.
[them] It passes the term faster than sitting.
[us] Well, we're glad of the hands.
[them] Some of your people watch me as if I'll run.
[us] They'll stop, given time.
[them] Let them watch, I gave my word.
[us] Do you ever think of just walking home?
[them,their:tribal] Never, it would shame the chief who gave me.
[them,their:medieval] My name was spoken before witnesses, I'd sooner lose a hand.
[them,their:hightech] I signed my name to the terms, and I read them first.
[them] No, I won't be the one who breaks my people's word.
[us] I didn't think so, but I had to ask.
[them] The nights are the long part of a term.
[us] Come and sit up with us, someone's always awake.
[them] I might, if your people don't mind a hostage in the room.
[them] When the fighting started, I didn't know whether to stand with you or keep away.
[us,trait:Brawler] Stand with us, next time, you've eaten our bread.
[us] Keep away, next time, your people would never forgive us if you fell.
[them] I'll remember that.
[us] Would your people really come if we called on the pact?
[them] They gave me so you'd believe they would.
[us] That's a hard way to make a promise.
[them,their:lowtech] It's the oldest way there is.
[them] It's the one that gets believed.
[them] When the term is out, I think I'll miss some of you.
[us] Then come back, and not as a hostage.
[them] A hostage who visits by choice, now that would be a story.
[them] My people broke their word, and I'm the one standing here.
[us] It isn't your doing.
[them,their:lowtech] It's my neck all the same, that's what a hostage is for.
[them] It's my neck all the same.
[them] Whatever your council decides, you've treated me fairly.
[us] I hope the council does the same.
[them] So do I, and I won't hold it against you if it doesn't.
[them] Go on, then, lock me up and be done with it.
[us] That's not mine to decide.
[them] Does {HOSTAGE} work here, or sit about?
[us] Works, the same as anyone.
[them,their:empire] Then the colony has taught {HOSTAGE} more humility than the court ever did.
[them] Good, idle hands make long days.
[us] Does {HOSTAGE} at least have a decent bed?
[them,their:tribal] A place at the fire, the same as any of us.
[them,their:hightech] A room, and a door that locks from the inside.
[them] A bed and a roof, and people who leave them be.
[them] {HOSTAGE} has made friends among us, you know.
[us] That sounds like {HOSTAGE}.
[them] We'll be sorry to send them back when the term is out.
[us] Is {HOSTAGE} being treated decently?
[them] Better than your colony treated its word.
[them] Your colony can still have {HOSTAGE} back, if it makes it worth our while.
[us] Then we'll find what it's worth.
[them] Sooner is better, for {HOSTAGE}'s sake.
[them] The last one of ours you kept came home well, so we worry less about {HOSTAGE}.
[us] We'll send {HOSTAGE} home the same way.
[us] Do your people often give hostages?
[them,their:tribal] When two clans make peace, one of the chief's kin goes to live at the other's fire.
[them,their:medieval] Hostages are exchanged before witnesses, and the priest writes the names down.
[them,their:industrial] We'd call it a guarantor, and there's a clause in the contract for it.
[them,their:empire] Hostages of rank are an old custom at court, and an honorable one.
[them,their:spacer,!their:empire] A guarantor is posted, and both sides log the terms.
[them] Only when the word alone isn't trusted.
[us] So, often enough.
